newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel holds key lending rate for June.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel holds key lending rate for June.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Monday it was holding its key lending rate for June at an annualised 13.9 percent.
The rate is the one charged commercial banks at daily and weekly monetary tenders.
The Bank of Israel last cut the base rate at the end of February to 13.9 percent and has held it at that level since then. In the preceding seven months, cuts totalled 3.1 percentage points.

The central bank said it decided to hold the line on interest rates for another month because actual inflation and inflationary expectations were at the upper limit of the government's target of seven to 10 percent for 1997.
The April consumer price index was a low 0.7 percent but it followed three months of big increases. The annualised inflation rate for the first four months of the year was about 10 percent.
In the local bond market, prices reflect inflationary expectations over the next 12 months of about 9.25 percent.
The bank said it recognised that a slowing economy could justify an interest rate cut, but it apparently gave a greater weighting to inflation figures.
Financial markets were expected to respond negatively to the decision.
Economists had predicted a cut of up to 0.5 point for June but warned that the bank might take a hard line and hold rates.

"The decision was disappointing. We were waiting for a symbolic rate cut of up to 0.3 point," said Yosi Weidelfield of Eyal Securities. "The market is expected to open lower (on Tuesday). The (Maof) options that were still trading after the announcment reflected expectations for a moderate decline."
Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House said: "I expect the stock market to open with some surplus supply tomorrow and prices of unlinked bonds and Makams will be lower."
He said the market had expected a reduction.
"I think (the Bank of Israel's) policy is right, but maybe this time it could have been a bit more flexible," Weisberg said.
